basis: Scheduled hours come from the current revision of each schedule (its rotations and overrides) and current membership, over the cohort range up to the observation time. They are scheduled hours, not worked hours.

Earlier schedule revisions are not retained, so a schedule change recomputes past scheduled hours; the schedule revisions used are listed. A slot held by a member who is now inactive or not a responder counts as uncovered.

Erased declaration cases have unknown acknowledgment state, shown separately from unacknowledged incidents. Shares use only observed retained acknowledgments; no erased case is attributed or treated as zero.
Load is the first explicit acknowledgement of each cohort incident, the entry acknowledgement time is measured to. Unacknowledged incidents are counted as unattributed, never assigned to anyone.

Load is normalised by scheduled primary hours, the role a page reaches first; backup hours are shown separately. Load to coverage is the share of acknowledgements divided by the share of primary hours: 1 means load in proportion to coverage. Without primary hours no rate is given.
Outside coverage counts acknowledgements made while the responder held neither primary nor backup on a schedule of that incident's service. Overlapping schedules count each hour once.
Teams are not modelled yet, so load is broken out by responder and by service.

Reassignment latency and after-hours interruptions are unavailable. Coverage hours are scheduled from current schedules, not worked hours (see the load basis).
Imported-history provenance is unavailable; timeline source kind describes representation, not native versus imported origin.
Source-reported recovery is what the monitoring sources reported, as accepted by Oncall; neither it nor a human attestation is independent verification of recovery.

Explicitly erased incidents retain only an anonymous declaration case with service and timestamp: all durations are unknown and the denominator stays visible. Earlier erasures made before this capability cannot be reconstructed. Unassignable declaration timestamps are separately counted.

basis: Scheduled hours come from the current revision of each schedule (its rotations and overrides) and current membership, over the cohort range up to the observation time. They are scheduled hours, not worked hours.

Earlier schedule revisions are not retained, so a schedule change recomputes past scheduled hours; the schedule revisions used are listed. A slot held by a member who is now inactive or not a responder counts as uncovered.

Erased declaration cases have unknown acknowledgment state, shown separately from unacknowledged incidents. Shares use only observed retained acknowledgments; no erased case is attributed or treated as zero.
Load is the first explicit acknowledgement of each cohort incident, the entry acknowledgement time is measured to. Unacknowledged incidents are counted as unattributed, never assigned to anyone.

Load is normalised by scheduled primary hours, the role a page reaches first; backup hours are shown separately. Load to coverage is the share of acknowledgements divided by the share of primary hours: 1 means load in proportion to coverage. Without primary hours no rate is given.
Outside coverage counts acknowledgements made while the responder held neither primary nor backup on a schedule of that incident's service. Overlapping schedules count each hour once.
Teams are not modelled yet, so load is broken out by responder and by service.

noise.definition: Alerts with a trigger event accepted in the cohort range [from,to), suppressed alerts included. An alert repeats when it has more than one trigger in range; a source/service/key is noisy when it repeats or opens more than one alert generation in range. The 20 noisiest keys are listed; the counts cover all of them.

cohort.inclusion: createdAt declaration in UTC [from,to); every matching incident retained regardless of state, severity, service configuration or metric availability; endpoints observed through generatedAt

definitions.mtta: Declaration to first explicit acknowledgement; resolution never implies acknowledgement
definitions.mttr: Declaration to final resolution; unresolved incidents are right-censored at generatedAt
definitions.recovery: Declaration to last evidenced human recovery attestation after any later mitigation; not independently verified recovery
definitions.sourceRecovery: Declaration to acceptance of the last recovery event reported by the sources of every linked alert; censored while a linked alert is active, unknown without linked alerts
definitions.statistics: Seconds; mean and nearest-rank p50/p90/p95 use measured values only. Total, measured, censored and unknown denominators remain visible. Histogram buckets are [fromSeconds,toSeconds), null upper bound means infinity
definitions.censored: Seconds is an observed lower bound, not a completed duration; source identifies the declaration entry
definitions.unknown: Seconds is null; no zero imputation. Invalid, future or pre-declaration endpoint timestamps are unknown
